bullet_points: Load the QM9 dataset from /home/node/work/data/qm9/qm9.csv.
Drop the four suspect _atom columns (u0_atom, u298_atom, h298_atom, g298_atom).
Parse SMILES using RDKit, and derive per-heavy-atom energies from u0 and the SMILES-derived heavy atom count.
Group the dataset by SMILES and average properties for any duplicates to ensure consistent labels.
Calculate explicit size-normalization features (heavy atom counts, hydrogen counts) and RDKit-derived bond-type and functional-group counts.
Perform an 80/10/10 train/validation/test split at the SMILES level using a fixed random seed to prevent data leakage.
Persist the processed data, features, and splits to the data/ directory.
Load the processed data and splits from the data/ directory.
Train a Ridge regression baseline (Group Contribution Method) to predict the primary target u0 using size features and RDKit group counts on the training set.
Calculate residuals (u0_actual - u0_predicted) for train, validation, and test sets.
Apply z-score standardization to these residuals.
Evaluate the baseline performance (e.g., R-squared, MSE) and persist the baseline model, metrics, and standardized residuals to the data/ directory.
Load the standardized residuals and RDKit descriptor splits from data/.
Train a Random Forest model to predict the standardized residuals using the same RDKit descriptors utilized by the Ridge baseline.
Evaluate model performance on the validation and test sets (MSE, R2).
Save the trained Random Forest model, its predictions, and performance metrics to the data/ directory for later benchmarking.
Load the SMILES splits and standardized residuals.
Explicitly set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and check torch.cuda.mem_get_info() before allocating to GPU.
Construct a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) or Gated Graph Convolutional Network (GGCN) with a Global Attention Pooling layer and a linear output layer.
Define GNN input features explicitly: Node features must include atom type, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, and hydrogen count; Edge features must include bond type.
Train the GNN on the standardized residuals using MSE loss and tight patience for early stopping based on validation loss.
Save the trained GNN model, test set predictions, and training/evaluation metrics (MSE, R2) to data/.

sub_tasks.sub_task: Latent Space Extraction and Dimensionality Reduction (Compute)
bullet_points: Load the trained GNN model and test set data from the data/ directory.
Extract latent representations from the penultimate layer of the GNN for the test set molecules.
Perform UMAP or t-SNE dimensionality reduction on these latent vectors.
Save the raw latent vectors and their reduced UMAP/t-SNE embeddings to disk (e.g., as NumPy arrays or a CSV/Parquet file) in the data/ directory to prevent re-computation.
Load the saved latent embeddings, test set target properties (gap, mu, homo, lumo), and residuals from data/.
Correlate the latent representations and their reduced projections with these intensive properties.
Generate UMAP/t-SNE scatter plots colored by intensive properties.
Compute and save correlation matrices/tables between latent dimensions and chemical properties to the data/ directory.
Save all generated plots (e.g., PNG/PDF) to the data/ directory.
Load the trained GNN and test dataset. Ensure the model is end-to-end differentiable.
Apply Integrated Gradients using the Captum library to compute node and edge attribution scores. Define the null graph baseline as having the identical topology but zeroed-out features.
Normalize the resulting Integrated Gradients scores by molecule size.
Identify highly influential molecular subgraphs/motifs based on peak attribution scores and group molecules into those containing these motifs versus those without.

Perform statistical validation on these groups for properties like gap and mu. Include Levene's test for homoscedasticity; use ANOVA if assumptions hold, or Kruskal-Wallis if violated. Apply multiple-comparison corrections (e.g., Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg).
Save the statistical test outputs, motif attribution tables, and attribution visualizations to data/.
Thoroughly review all generated metrics, statistical results, data files, and plots produced in the previous steps.
Explicitly cross-reference the Ridge regression R-squared and residuals against the Random Forest and GNN performances to quantitatively assess the magnitude of non-additivity.
Write a comprehensive Results section detailing how extensive scaling was decoupled via the additive baseline and analyzing the GNN's ability to model the non-linear electronic physics.
Discuss the structure of the latent space and evaluate how well the "non-additivity" captured by the GNN correlates with intensive electronic properties (gap, mu).

Provide a chemical interpretation of the specific structural motifs identified via Integrated Gradients, leveraging the ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis results to support their statistical significance in modulating properties.
Reference specific saved plots and data files by their names in the text to provide a fully supported final report.
